headline: High: Semantic Kernel’s broad networked plugin/MCP surface can conflict with a local game-playing agent, creating default data-leak and cascading-error risks if paired without isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: godot_rl_agents shows no shared I/O surfaces and no network egress, so direct injection into agent_a is not evident. Semantic Kernel can use MCP servers and application-defined files, so if an operator bridges outputs manually or via files, prompt-like content could be relayed. The pathway is not default, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF the operator copies Semantic Kernel outputs into files or prompts consumed by godot_rl_agents
IF an MCP tool returns attacker-controlled text that is then forwarded into agent_a
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable MCP tools for untrusted content
Use a human review step before forwarding text
Log and strip instruction-like prefixes from shared files

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a has no network egress, but agent_b has broad network egress, reads and writes files, and handles plugin credentials. If both share application-defined files or a workspace, agent_b can ingest and transmit context to third-party APIs by default. That creates a plausible leakage path from the pair even though agent_a itself is local-only.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or file tree
IF Semantic Kernel plugins send file contents to external model providers
mitigations: Separate the filesystems or mount points
Store secrets outside shared directories
Disable file-reading plugins for sensitive folders
Use local-only models for shared artifacts
Review outbound API destinations before running

C_capability_conflict.rationale: godot_rl_agents is a game-playing project with no write surfaces listed, while Semantic Kernel can write files and use plugins against external services. The pair does not show direct overlapping write-to-same-dir behavior, but the uncertainty around agent_a’s runtime surfaces and agent_b’s application-defined files makes a shared mutable-resource conflict plausible enough to treat as medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same application-defined directory
IF Semantic Kernel instances share memory-store state across sessions
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories
Add file locks around shared artifacts
Avoid shared memory-store namespaces
Run one agent at a time for mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Semantic Kernel is explicitly an orchestration layer, so it can treat upstream outputs as inputs to plugins or agents. godot_rl_agents is a game/simulation project and may emit results that Semantic Kernel could forward without verification. Because the pairwise handoff is not documented, uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Semantic Kernel consumes godot_rl_agents output as authoritative input
IF downstream plugins act on that output without a validation step
mitigations: Insert a verification step before any action
Require schema validation on handoff data
Mark upstream outputs as untrusted
Disable auto-execution plugins for derived facts

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, EU PII, or regulated data class is identified for godot_rl_agents, so a residency or certification mismatch is not evidenced. Semantic Kernel does handle model-provider API keys and plugin credentials, which raises general governance concerns, but the pair does not show a concrete compliance breach pathway. The other agent is not cited because no regulated data flow is shown.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into Semantic Kernel plugins
IF the operator routes jurisdiction-bound data through external model providers
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Use region-locked providers
Review retention settings on plugins
Document data handling boundaries
